cards.title: Payment and Checkout Compliance Checks for GMC
cards.summary: Test payment methods, final price transparency, and discount codes on your checkout, because GMC bots audit all three.
cards.use_when: Preparing or auditing your store checkout to avoid Google Merchant Center suspension or promotion disapproval.

cards.title: Listing Accuracy Checklist: Claims, Reviews, Links, Pricing
cards.summary: Make listing claims factual, reviews authentic, links correct and listed prices match checkout to prevent GMC misrepresentation flags.
cards.use_when: Auditing product listings and product pages before scaling Google Shopping or PMax spend.

cards.title: Branding, Navigation and Legal Page Checks for GMC
cards.summary: Polish brand assets, keep footer links working and update legal pages to look like a reputable store in Google's eyes.
cards.use_when: Cleaning up store branding, navigation and policy pages so GMC bots see a trusted store.

cards.title: Shipping, Returns and Contact Info Sync for GMC
cards.summary: Keep shipping costs, courier details, returns policy and contact info synchronized between your site and GMC and review them monthly.
cards.use_when: Setting up or maintaining shipping, returns and contact sections to prevent GMC suspension.

cards.title: Site Speed, Design and App Health as GMC Trust Signals
cards.summary: Fast, well-branded sites with working apps get better CPCs and store ratings; slow or broken stores risk GMC penalties.
cards.use_when: Improving site experience to protect Google Ads performance and Merchant Center standing.

cards.title: The 34-Item GMC Anti-Suspension Checklist by Frequency
cards.summary: Work a 34-point Google Merchant Center checklist split into daily, weekly, monthly and one-time tasks to avoid suspension.
cards.use_when: Building an ongoing ops routine for your Google Merchant Center account.

cards.title: Build a Reusable Brand Context Profile with AI Before Writing Ad Copy
cards.summary: Train an LLM on your brand and product page to produce a reusable context profile for ads, landing pages and emails.
cards.use_when: Preparing to generate Google Ads assets, Meta copy, landing page copy or emails and needing consistent brand context.

cards.title: Use AI Deep Research to Build Customer and Market Understanding
cards.summary: Run a deep research prompt in a research-capable model with your URL and product PDF to produce a long brand, audience and market brief.
cards.use_when: Replacing or supplementing weeks of manual customer and market research before writing ads or landing pages.

cards.title: Convert Research into JSON Context Profiles for Consistent Copy
cards.summary: Use an LLM to turn deep research into avatar, market and brand JSON profiles plus one combined context file.
cards.use_when: Structuring brand research so any AI session can instantly understand your store before generating copy.

cards.title: Generate All Google Ads Assets from a Context Profile
cards.summary: Paste your brand context plus a Google Ads JSON asset template into an LLM to produce RSA headlines, descriptions, sitelinks, callouts, snippets and PMax assets.
cards.use_when: Building Google Search or PMax campaign assets at scale without starting from a blank page.

cards.title: Set Up a Branded Search Campaign to Protect and Capture Demand
cards.summary: Run a search campaign on exact-match brand terms with impression-share bidding to own the SERP, defend against competitors and feed cheap conversion data.
cards.use_when: Launching or optimizing paid search on your own brand name to capture searchers who saw you elsewhere.

cards.title: Why Every Ecommerce Brand Should Run a Branded Search Campaign
cards.summary: Branded search ads expand your SERP footprint, defend your brand from competitors and load cheap high-intent conversion data into your account.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to spend on your own brand terms in Google Ads.

cards.title: Set Up and Automate a Branded Shopping Campaign with Scripts
cards.summary: Create a Shopping campaign limited to branded terms and use scripts to automatically exclude non-branded search queries.
cards.use_when: Adding a high-leverage, fast-to-launch Shopping campaign to lift account efficiency and cheap sales.

cards.title: Branded Search & Shopping Campaigns: Structure, Bidding & Exclusions
cards.summary: Build a manual-CPC branded shopping campaign plus branded search to protect your brand term, harvest cheap conversions and keep prospecting bids clean.
cards.use_when: Setting up or auditing paid search structure for a store that already gets branded searches and wants brand protection plus cheaper conversion data.

cards.title: Cold Search Campaigns: Capture Problem-Aware Demand, Not Product-Aware Demand
cards.summary: Use broad-match cold search ads on problem-aware queries to reach people who don't know your brand, then tighten winners into exact match.
cards.use_when: Planning acquisition for a store whose product solves a specific problem and whose product-aware search demand is exhausted or too expensive.

cards.title: Build Mini-Funnels Per Search Term for Cold Traffic
cards.summary: Match one landing page and one ad per high-volume problem-aware search phrase to convert cold searchers you already know are looking for.
cards.use_when: Deciding how many landing pages to build for paid search and where to spend page-creation effort on problem-aware traffic.

cards.title: Performance Max: What It Is and Where It Fits in the Google Funnel
cards.summary: Treat Performance Max as a middle-of-funnel catch-all engine fed by signals, not a hands-off campaign that replaces search, shopping or YouTube.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to add Performance Max to a store's Google account and what budget share and role to assign it.

cards.title: Qualify Your Store for Performance Max Before Launching
cards.summary: Screen for feed quality, tracking, budget and conversion volume before committing a store to Performance Max.
cards.use_when: Assessing whether a store is ready for Performance Max or should stay on manual search and manual shopping.

cards.title: Set Up a Performance Max Campaign: Bidding, Locations, Devices, Exclusions
cards.summary: Configure a Performance Max campaign with the right bidding strategy, location targeting, device set and brand exclusions.
cards.use_when: Building a new Performance Max campaign inside a Google Ads account.

cards.title: Structure Performance Max Around Signal Density, Not Campaign Count
cards.summary: Segment Performance Max by product category and country so signals concentrate in one campaign per audience type.
cards.use_when: Deciding how many Performance Max campaigns a store should run and how to split products and geographies.

cards.title: Select Products for Performance Max: Scalers, Zombie Asset Groups and 80/20
cards.summary: Choose the products Performance Max focuses on using the 80/20 principle, and quarantine underperformers instead of letting them dilute spend.
cards.use_when: Building or pruning the product list inside a Performance Max campaign.

cards.title: Handle Performance Max's Reporting, Placement and CPC Limitations
cards.summary: Mitigate Performance Max's attribution credit, placement leakage and uncontrolled CPC with third-party measurement, audits and exclusions.
cards.use_when: Auditing an existing Performance Max campaign for wasted spend or unreliable reporting.

cards.title: Audience Signals and Conversion Data Are the Real Performance Max Inputs
cards.summary: Supply customer lists, in-market and custom-intent audiences plus clean conversion tracking so Performance Max can start without a learning plateau.
cards.use_when: Launching a Performance Max campaign from a cold start or improving an underperforming one by changing its inputs.

cards.title: Use Search Terms and Landing Page Audits to Fix Google Ads Waste
cards.summary: Regularly review search terms and landing pages to remove non-converting queries and unreviewed placements that drain budget.
cards.use_when: Running weekly/monthly maintenance on Google search, shopping or Performance Max campaigns.

cards.title: Performance Max campaign setup with category-specific asset groups
cards.summary: Build PMAX campaigns by splitting asset groups by product category, feeding Google matched headlines/imagery/landing pages, and using search and audience signals as a conversion flywheel.
cards.use_when: Launching or restructuring a Performance Max campaign for a store with multiple product categories (e.g. dresses, shoes, hats).

cards.title: Daily PMAX search-term and auction-insight hygiene
cards.summary: Review PMAX search-term insights every day to exclude irrelevant queries, catch branded leakage, and harvest new profitable keywords for search campaigns.
cards.use_when: Daily check on a running Performance Max campaign to protect budget and reallocate targeting.

cards.title: Weekly PMAX product-level spend and SKU exclusion
cards.summary: Inspect which products actually receive PMAX budget weekly and exclude poor-performing or out-of-stock SKUs to protect efficiency.
cards.use_when: Weekly budget review for a Performance Max campaign with multiple products or categories.

cards.title: Weekly asset and landing-page exclusions in PMAX
cards.summary: Refresh low-performing ad assets weekly and exclude non-converting URLs from final URL expansion to keep spend on sales pages.
cards.use_when: Weekly creative and traffic-routing review inside a live Performance Max campaign.

cards.title: Monthly PMAX search-theme and customer-list refresh
cards.summary: Once a month, replace non-converting search themes with proven converters and re-upload your first-party customer list to sharpen signal quality.
cards.use_when: Monthly optimization cycle for PMAX audience and keyword signals.

cards.title: Break-even CPA and ROAS as your scaling baseline
cards.summary: Calculate the maximum you can spend to acquire a customer (break-even CPA) and the corresponding break-even ROAS from your own unit economics before scaling any campaign.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether you can profitably increase Google Ads budget, bids or a new channel's spend.

cards.title: Weekly budget scaling rules with traffic-light KPIs
cards.summary: Use break-even CPA and ROAS to scale winners 10–20%, cut losers fast, and judge whether to raise budget or lower targets based on budget pacing.
cards.use_when: Weekly budget and bid decisions across Google Ads campaigns including PMAX.

cards.title: Device and placement rules for PMAX and demand gen
cards.summary: Turn off tablets always, keep mobile (highest-converting, highest-cost) and desktop on, and reserve TV placements for dedicated demand-gen campaigns.
cards.use_when: Setting device targeting for a Performance Max or demand-gen campaign.

cards.title: Where YouTube and demand gen sit in the Google Ads funnel
cards.summary: Structure campaigns as demand generation (top), prospecting search/shopping/PMAX (middle, capped by search volume), and branded/remarketing (bottom) so YouTube feeds the whole system.
cards.use_when: Auditing an account's campaign mix or deciding where to add YouTube/demand-gen spend.

cards.title: Why YouTube ads scale past search-volume ceilings
cards.summary: Use YouTube demand gen for ecommerce when search/shopping demand is capped or CPCs are inflating, exploiting cheap CPM arbitrage and creative reuse.
cards.use_when: Evaluating whether to open a new acquisition channel because search/shopping volume or margin is maxed out.

cards.title: Choosing the right YouTube placement: Shorts, in-stream or in-feed
cards.summary: Start with YouTube Shorts and in-stream for volume and testing; treat in-feed as a later, higher-production placement.
cards.use_when: Allocating YouTube demand-gen budget across placements for an ecommerce brand.

cards.title: YouTube in-stream creative structure and first 5 seconds
cards.summary: Because skipped in-stream ads guarantee only 5 seconds, front-load an audio+visual movie-trailer hook, then demo, social proof and a strong CTA to beat 1% CTR.
cards.use_when: Writing or editing YouTube in-stream ad creative for a cold ecommerce audience.

cards.title: YouTube as brand-lift and TV-reach play
cards.summary: Use demand-gen YouTube placements partly for perceived legitimacy and TV reach, accepting view-through rather than direct-click conversions.
cards.use_when: Justifying and measuring upper-funnel YouTube spend for a brand that mostly converts later through search.

cards.title: Composite approach: standard shopping alongside PMAX
cards.summary: Test running standard shopping at a low tROAS with PMAX as a higher-tROAS catch-all, and mirror PMAX conversion data into dedicated search campaigns.
cards.use_when: Considering advanced Google Ads structures after a PMAX campaign has conversion data.

cards.title: Demand Gen Campaign Setup for YouTube Cold Traffic
cards.summary: Step-by-step Google Ads demand gen campaign configuration for running YouTube in-stream and Shorts as cold-traffic acquisition.
cards.use_when: Launching your first YouTube/Demand Gen cold-traffic campaign in Google Ads and you need the exact settings to configure.

cards.title: Video Upload and Ad Group Structure for YouTube Ads
cards.summary: How to structure video ad groups and upload videos so you can test concepts and graduate winners into dedicated ad groups.
cards.use_when: Setting up the video/creative layer of a YouTube demand gen campaign and deciding how to organize ad groups.

cards.title: The Six YouTube Ad KPIs and Their Ranges
cards.summary: Track six metrics — view rate, CTR, conversion rate, new customer CPA, new customer ROAS, view-through conversions — with rough good/bad ranges.
cards.use_when: Reviewing performance of a running YouTube/Demand Gen cold-traffic campaign and deciding whether to keep, pause or scale an ad.

cards.title: Traffic Scaling Rules: When to Pause, Keep or Scale an Ad
cards.summary: Decision rules for pausing, holding or scaling a YouTube ad based on combined view rate, CTR, conversion and new customer CPA performance.
cards.use_when: Evaluating individual YouTube ad creatives to decide pause/continue/scale in a cold-traffic campaign.

cards.title: Segment Branded vs Non-Branded Campaigns
cards.summary: Separate branded search/shopping from cold non-branded campaigns so paid spend isn't credited with traffic organic or Meta already generated.
cards.use_when: Auditing or structuring a Google Ads account, especially for brands with existing organic or Meta-driven branded search demand.

cards.title: Problem-Aware Creative vs Demographic Targeting on YouTube
cards.summary: Write YouTube hooks that call out the situation a problem-aware viewer is in rather than a demographic, to stay compliant and unlock broad YouTube inventory.
cards.use_when: Writing or briefing YouTube ad hooks and creative for a cold-traffic e-commerce product, especially a health/supplement/wellness offer.

cards.title: Choose Conversion Mechanisms in Order of Proven Performance
cards.summary: The source's ordered list of YouTube conversion mechanisms — decked-out sales page first, then advertorial/quiz, then VSSL and listicles at scale.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to send YouTube cold traffic and which landing page/conversion mechanism to test for a Direct-to-Consumer product.

cards.title: Set Up a New-Customer Conversion Tag
cards.summary: Install two purchase tags — a standard purchase tag plus a custom event that only fires on first order — and optimize around the new-customer event.
cards.use_when: Setting up conversion tracking for Google Ads on a store where you want to optimize for new customers rather than all purchasers.

cards.title: Google Ads Budget Allocation: 80/20 for Meta-Heavy Brands
cards.summary: For a Meta-heavy direct-response brand, allocate ~80% of Google budget to Demand Gen/YouTube cold traffic and cap search/shopping/brand.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to split Google Ads budget across campaign types for a brand whose acquisition is predominantly creative-led cold traffic.

cards.title: Demand Gen as the Cold-Traffic Engine for Meta-Heavy Brands
cards.summary: Why direct-response brands should prioritize Demand Gen/YouTube over Pmax/search for cold traffic, and when search/shopping still fits.
cards.use_when: Choosing Google campaign type for a cold-traffic e-commerce acquisition push.

cards.title: PMAX for a Single Hero Product
cards.summary: Why you can run one PMAX campaign for a single hero product instead of splitting into many campaigns, and how to feed it signal.
cards.use_when: Structuring Google Ads for a store built around one hero product/SKU.

cards.title: Compliance and Landing Page Prep Before Running YouTube Ads
cards.summary: Make ads, pages and product pages compliant before launching YouTube cold traffic so ads get approved and the account stays live.
cards.use_when: Preparing a health/supplement/wellness (or otherwise restricted-category) store to launch YouTube/Google ads.

cards.title: Retain YouTube Cold Traffic With Email Capture and Flows
cards.summary: Capture YouTube visitors with a popup, then run a deep welcome flow and post-purchase/replenishment sequence to extend LTV.
cards.use_when: Planning the retention and LTV layer behind a cold-traffic YouTube campaign to make acquisition economics work.

cards.title: Post-Click Landing Page Structure for YouTube Cold Traffic
cards.summary: Build a long, educational landing page with above-the-fold benefits plus stacked proof sections to convert cold YouTube traffic at ~2%.
cards.use_when: Designing or auditing the landing page that YouTube cold traffic is sent to and trying to lift conversion rate beyond ~0.05%.

cards.title: Consolidate Performance Max for high signal density
cards.summary: Concentrate cold-traffic spend into one PMax campaign so Google gets dense conversion signals rather than fragmented ones.
cards.use_when: Setting up or restructuring Google Ads account structure for a store's cold acquisition, deciding whether to split one PMax campaign into many.

cards.title: Rebuild the PDP as a direct-response cold-traffic page
cards.summary: Convert an educational or bare product page into a structured persuasion flow that can sell unfamiliar cold visitors, not just loyal repeat buyers.
cards.use_when: A store is scaling into new audiences and its current PDP converts returning customers but stalls cold traffic.

cards.title: Build the full cold-traffic conversion mechanism, not just ads
cards.summary: Treat the ads, pre-sale page, PDP, order flow and after-sell as one system, because the page that receives the click determines whether the ad spend converts.
cards.use_when: Planning a cold acquisition push and deciding which assets must be built or fixed before raising spend.

cards.title: Design an objection-handling block sequence on the PDP
cards.summary: Build a PDP section order that moves a cold visitor from 'what is this' through objections, proof, comparison, then offer.
cards.use_when: Merchandising a PDP for a supplement, wellness or other considered-purchase product where cold visitors need convincing.

cards.title: Monitor the ad account daily to catch demand spikes
cards.summary: Check spend and impression behavior every day so search demand spikes from external events can be funded within hours, not missed.
cards.use_when: Running Google Ads for a category that can be featured in podcasts, news or social media and may spike suddenly.

cards.title: Run 30/60/90/180/365-day contribution math before deciding how much to pay per customer
cards.summary: Decide how aggressively to buy customers using long-window contribution data, not front-end profit on the first order.
cards.use_when: Setting target CPA, deciding whether to accept near break-even or loss-making first orders to win market share in a repeat-purchase category.

cards.title: Position 'RoRoaWAS' correctly: low is the goal
cards.summary: Understand that in this source's framing, a lower return-on-ad-spend-in-relation-to-a-window metric means faster payback, so low values are desirable.
cards.use_when: Reviewing ad reporting and reacting to a metric that looks counterintuitively weak or strong.

cards.title: Use YouTube as the scaling lever once search and shopping plateau
cards.summary: Add YouTube to the cold-traffic mix when search and shopping demand is fully captured, because it adds new top-of-funnel inventory.
cards.use_when: Google search, shopping and display spend has hit a ceiling and the store needs new cold audience volume.

cards.title: Plan for creative volume to beat ad platform compliance filters
cards.summary: For regulated categories, build a creative production pipeline that produces enough compliant variants to find the few that both pass policy and convert.
cards.use_when: Running health, wellness or supplement ads on Google where policy review rejects most creative angles that work on Meta.

cards.title: Set the LTV engine: front-end acquisition campaigns feeding email/SMS and upsells
cards.summary: Structure paid campaigns and retention flows as one engine where acquisition buys first orders and email, SMS and upsells produce the repeat value.
cards.use_when: Designing the relationship between acquisition campaigns and retention channels to justify higher cold-traffic spend.

cards.title: Differentiate a PDP when competitors enter a validated category
cards.summary: When a category gets public attention and competitors flood in, replace first-mover advantage with evidence, clarity and differentiation on the page.
cards.use_when: A store's product category is being talked about publicly and new competitors are launching similar products.

cards.title: Start Google Ads with Search and Shopping, add Performance Max later
cards.summary: Sequence Google Ads campaign types for an ecommerce store by beginning with intuitive Search and Shopping campaigns and only layering in Performance Max once the account holds enough purchase data.
cards.use_when: Deciding which Google Ads campaign types to launch first for a store, or judging whether the account is ready for Performance Max.

cards.title: Concentrate cold-traffic spend on one or a few winning products
cards.summary: Focus Google Ads budget on the small number of SKUs that acquire cold-audience customers cheaply instead of spreading spend thinly across the whole catalog.
cards.use_when: Structuring Google Ads campaigns and budget allocation across a multi-SKU catalog, especially when prospecting to cold audiences.

cards.title: Open up the full catalog only for warm and remarketing audiences
cards.summary: Use dynamic product catalog ads and remarketing to show warm visitors the exact products they engaged with, while selling the wider range to people already in the ecosystem.
cards.use_when: Building Google Ads remarketing and dynamic product ad campaigns for site visitors and past customers, or deciding which SKUs to show which audience.

cards.title: Know AOV, margin and LTV before setting an allowable CAC
cards.summary: Calculate the unit economics that determine what the store can afford to pay to acquire a customer, using AOV, gross margin and lifetime value together.
cards.use_when: Setting target CPA/ROAS for Google Ads, deciding whether a campaign can be profitable, or diagnosing why acquisition costs feel unaffordable.

cards.title: Raise allowable acquisition cost by improving LTV rather than shaving CPA
cards.summary: Grow customer lifetime value to justify a far higher cost per acquisition, prioritising scale and repeat purchase over small percentage cuts to CPA.
cards.use_when: Setting CPC/CPA ceilings, deciding whether to run ads at a temporarily unprofitable ROAS, or prioritising between conversion-rate tweaks and retention improvements.

cards.title: Use a free-plus-shipping or generous front-end offer to acquire at scale
cards.summary: Apply reciprocity by giving a desirable entry product away for the cost of shipping, then monetise the natural follow-on purchases the customer will need.
cards.use_when: Designing a new-customer acquisition offer or entry-point product for cold Google Ads traffic.

cards.title: Discount tactically instead of defaulting to blanket sales
cards.summary: Preserve gross profit by targeting discounts at high-margin products or AOV thresholds rather than running deep storewide sales that trigger a race to the bottom.
cards.use_when: Planning seasonal promotions, Google Ads offer messaging, or a discount-led acquisition campaign.

cards.title: Mine customer reviews to write ad copy and find product fixes
cards.summary: Turn five-star review language into ad copy and creative, and use negative reviews to spot product and fulfilment problems.
cards.use_when: Writing Google Ads copy and creative for an ecommerce product, or looking for product/fulfilment improvements.

cards.title: Fix the campaign before increasing budget — ROAS falls as spend rises
cards.summary: Scale only from a profitable position, because Google serves the best prospects first and return on ad spend declines as budgets grow.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to raise Google Ads budget on an underperforming campaign, or planning a scaling sequence for a store.

cards.title: Track cross-platform attribution before trusting platform-reported results
cards.summary: Maintain independent attribution across ad channels and organic traffic so you know where purchases actually originate before making budget decisions.
cards.use_when: Setting up measurement for a Google Ads programme that also runs other paid channels or earns organic traffic.

cards.title: Build founder visibility and tell the product origin story
cards.summary: Use a founder personal brand or, at minimum, the product's origin story as a trust asset that lifts Google Ads performance.
cards.use_when: Developing brand positioning and ad creative for an ecommerce store, or deciding whether to invest in founder-led content.

cards.title: Why your ad creative—not your targeting—selects the buyer
cards.summary: Meta's system replaced interest/lookalike labels with vector-based targeting, so audience selection now happens through your creative and the algorithm's clustering.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to allocate budget between targeting settings and creative production, or when an agency proposes rebuilding interest and lookalike ad sets.

cards.title: The three-stage Meta delivery pipeline: retrieval, ranking, auction
cards.summary: Every impression passes through retrieval (Andromeda shortlisting from tens of millions of ads), ranking (relevance scoring), then the auction, all in roughly 200 milliseconds.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing why ads get no delivery or poor performance, or deciding whether a change targets creative, structure, or bid.

cards.title: Trigger creative fatigue deliberately, then refresh before ROAS tapers
cards.summary: Very specific persona-callout ads saturate their cluster fast, after which Meta either re-serves the same people or drifts outside your ICP and ROAS declines.
cards.use_when: Planning creative refresh cadence, or explaining declining ROAS and rising frequency on a narrowly targeted persona-based ad.

cards.title: Use exclusions to stop budget leaking to your warm customer cluster
cards.summary: Meta preferentially serves ads to warm clusters already likely to convert, so if you don't exclude existing customers, the algorithm will spend on people who would have bought anyway.
cards.use_when: Setting up a new broad-targeting campaign or auditing whether reported conversion efficiency is inflated by existing customers.

cards.title: Bid equation: relevance multipliers beat raising bids
cards.summary: Placement goes to Bid × Estimated Action Rate + Ad Quality, so a lower bidder with superior relevance can beat you—being more relevant is the faster route to cheaper delivery.
cards.use_when: Considering whether to raise bids to win more auctions, or diagnosing why a competitor wins placements at a lower apparent cost.

cards.title: Turn estimated action rate into a CPM arbitrage through landing-page action design
cards.summary: The source reports that high-action landing experiences correlate with far lower CPMs, suggesting you can design for a high action rate to reduce what you pay for delivery.
cards.use_when: Designing or comparing landing pages, lead capture, or checkout flows where you want to lower effective ad costs.
